title: Stop counting Hyprland virtual outputs as external monitors
author: HritwikSinghal
body:
Fixes #8027.

## What goes wrong

Dock the laptop, turn the laptop screen off (SUPER + CTRL + Delete, or Hardware -> Laptop Display), then unplug the external monitor. The laptop is left with no screen at all until the next login.

## Why

When the last enabled monitor goes away, Hyprland creates a placeholder output named FALLBACK (FallbackStateKeeper, src/state/FallbackState.cpp, since 0.56.0). Nothing is behind it, but it reports `disabled: false` and its name is not eDP/LVDS/DSI, so `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-external-active` answered "an external monitor is active".

Six callers use that answer to decide whether turning the laptop screen back on is safe, and all six back off: `off()` and `recover()` in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal`, `recover()` in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-internal-mirror`, `enable_internal()` and the dock check in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-clamshell`, and the poll in `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-watch`. Only the next login recovers it, because `omarchy-recover-internal-monitor.service` asks `omarchy-hw-external-monitors` instead, which reads the kernel.

## The fix

Ask the kernel too: a real display has a DRM connector, a placeholder has none. Fixing the helper fixes all six callers at once.

Excluding the names FALLBACK and HEADLESS-* would also work today, but 0.55 called this same output HEADLESS-n and 0.56 renamed it, so the next rename would bring the bug back with nothing to notice it.

`monitors all` stays, so a mirrored external keeps counting. Any connector status except `disconnected` counts, because a connector with no working detect (VGA, DVI-I) reports `unknown` for a display that is genuinely attached.

## Measured on hardware

Dell XPS, Intel Panther Lake, eDP-1 plus a Dell AW3225QF on DP-1. Omarchy 4.0.0, Hyprland 0.56.2. Sampled 5 times a second across a real unplug:

| | placeholder visible | toggle flag | laptop screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1.75s | stayed set | never came back on its own |
| after | under 0.5s | cleared by the next sample | back immediately |

## Tests

New `test/shell.d/monitor-external-active-test.sh`, 11 checks. Against the current helper it fails at the first one:

    not ok - the FALLBACK output is not counted as an external monitor

Full suite: 7 of 246 files fail, the same 7 that fail on a clean quattro checkout (see #7125).
